original_statement: MRAC extension: V = e'Pe + tr(K~' Gamma^-1 K~), V-dot = -e'Qe <= 0, so by LaSalle (e, K~) -> (0, 0); asymptotically stable (with sigma-modification Eq. 5.13)
verification_method: Mathematical review
findings_and_evidence: V-dot = -e'Qe only gives boundedness and, through Barbalat's lemma (the system is non-autonomous because of r(t)), e -> 0. Adding sigma-modification (5.13) adds -sigma tr(K~' Gamma^-1 K) to V-dot, so V-dot <= -e'Qe no longer holds (only uniform ultimate boundedness).
limitations: Textbook source (Ioannou & Sun, Robust Adaptive Control, 1996) identified but not examined
recommended_action: Withdraw or correct the stability statement

source_document: tests/test_controllers.py; evidence C26
original_statement: The scheduled controller is stable (frozen-time) for SoH in [0.5,1], gamma in [0,10]
verification_method: (i) Discrete slow-variation bound via the Lyapunov form of the DARE; (ii) search for a common quadratic Lyapunov function
findings_and_evidence: (i) Using A_cl'P A_cl - P = -(Q + K'RK) (residual 2e-13): sufficient condition |dSoH per 10 ms step| <= 3.15e-10, about 5x above a fast realistic drift (20 %/year). (ii) Stronger: P(SoH = 1) is a common Lyapunov function for all A_cl(SoH), SoH in [0.5,1] (1001-point grid), for gamma pairs (1,1), (0,5), (5,0), (5,5), (1,5), (5,1): max eig(A_cl'P1 A_cl - P1) = -1.26e-4 to -1.39e-4 (relative -2.2e-7 to -2.4e-7). So the linear closed loop is exponentially stable even under arbitrarily fast SoH variation in that range. Negative control (identity candidate) fails, as expected.
limitations: Linear design model; grid-based certificate (not a continuum proof); no saturation; small relative margin
recommended_action: Replace the thesis proof (TF-18) with this result and its scope

source_document: this audit (new deduction)
original_statement: Under the model's assumptions, two controllers that produce the same speed trajectory use exactly the same battery energy
required_assumptions: Constant efficiencies; no friction braking; rigid drivetrain; same SoH and parameters; F_w strictly increasing in t_s
verification_method: Inverse-dynamics argument plus independent numerical reference
findings_and_evidence: Given v(t), M_eff dv/dt + loads fixes F_w; F_w is a strictly increasing function of t_s, so T(t) = t_s + B_m w is unique. Then P_m, P_e, I(t), V1(t) and E_chem follow uniquely. Ideal-tracking energy: S1 49.714 (SoH 1.0) / 49.803 (SoH 0.8) Wh/km; S2 36.951 / 36.990 Wh/km. Simulated runs are 0.14-0.20 % higher.
limitations: Breaks once friction braking, efficiency maps or a DC-link torque limit are introduced
recommended_action: Add it to the thesis as the structural reason for the null result
